text: dsh-superagent 是把本机操作者需求交给 DSH 编排器的本地编码代理插件，支持 DSH 的 Web 管理面板。它把主会话中的用户消息转换为需求触发器，路由会话评估后建立工单，并由独立 Worker 会话在对应工作区执行，再把结果回复到原会话。每个工作区可有自己的主会话，也可携带图片和文件附件；面板可查看来源、工单、会话和运行状态，并管理提示词与设置。适合希望在本机工作区通过对话委派编码任务的 DSH 用户。需配置 DSH 及其模型和执行环境。

dsh-superagent is a DSH plugin that turns local chat requests into workspace tickets for worker sessions and relays results to the originating conversation. It supports per-workspace main sessions, file and image attachments, and a web panel for managing tickets, sessions, and prompts.
想把本机 DSH 对话里的编码需求交给独立工作会话处理。
能不能让每个工作区都有自己的任务编排会话？
希望代理在我的项目目录里执行任务，并把结果发回原对话。
怎么从 DSH 主会话委派一项编码工作？
I want to delegate a coding request from DSH chat to a worker in my workspace.
Can task results be sent back to the conversation that started the work?
dsh-superagent 的功能「本机对话转工单」：主会话中由用户发送的文本会转为需求触发器，经编排评估并进入工单流程；没有文字时也可用附件作为需求。
dsh-superagent 的功能「工作区主会话」：按工作区创建并记住主会话，需求在所属工作区路由，供用户分别委派任务。
dsh-superagent 的功能「独立 Worker 执行」：工单由持久的 Worker 会话和对应工作目录处理，执行报告再传回编排会话。
dsh-superagent 的功能「任务管理面板」：Web 管理面板提供工单、日志、设置、提示词和会话等 API，供操作者查看与管理。
我想把带图片或文件的任务交给工作区里的编码代理。
I need a panel to review and manage coding tasks handled by DSH workers.

dsh-superagent README · dsh-superagent：dsh-superagent is a proactive coding agent for one GitHub repository, packaged as a bundle for [DeepSeek Harness](https://www.deepseek.com/en/harness/). It listens to GitHub and, optionally, Feishu. When someone allowed asks the agent for work, it opens a work item, works on it in its own agent session and directory, and answers in the original conversation, for example with a pull request. A web panel shows what needs a person.

dsh-superagent README · This fork: work from your own machine：This repository is a fork of [dsh-superagent](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/dsh-superagent) that serves
**the person sitting at the machine** instead of a GitHub repository. Four things differ from upstream:
section: This fork: work from your own machine

text:
dsh-superagent README · This fork: work from your own machine：- **A local Source.** `src/sources/dsh.ts` (exported as `./local-watch`) turns a message in the main
  Session into a Trigger, and sends the answer back to that same Session. `source.kind === 'user'` is
  the filter, so messages that the orchestrator injects itself never loop back in.
- **One main Session per workspace.** Every sidebar workspace has its own orchestrator, created on
  demand and remembered in `KV.runtime.masters` (workspaceId to sessionId). `GET
  /orchestrator/api/master?workspace=<id>` returns it, creating it when missing.
- **A sidebar entry.** The client half injects a star button into each workspace group row
  (`[data-row-key^="workspace:"]`), opens that workspace's main Session, and hides main-session rows
  from the list.
- **Attachments.** Images and files travel with the request: the Trigger carries
  `meta.attachments`, and the Worker receives the attachment-store path so it can open the file
  before deciding anything.
section: This fork: work from your own machine

text:
dsh-superagent README · This fork: work from your own machine：It also runs without GitHub: `resolveDeployment` returns an empty repository when no remote is
configured, and the GitHub watcher reports `paused` instead of polling.

When an operator asks for work, the main Session routes it into a Ticket and a Worker does it in that
workspace's directory; the main Session never edits files itself.
section: This fork: work from your own machine

text: dsh-superagent README · This fork: work from your own machine：It is also a way of working with an agent: **take as little human attention as possible, and give as much value as possible.** An agent that can act for a whole team can also waste a whole team's attention, so it acts only when asked or when a rule the team wrote allows it, and speaks only when someone must act or can use a result. [docs/000-philosophy.md](docs/000-philosophy.md) explains the principle and what it asks of the operator.
section: This fork: work from your own machine

bundle used by `dsh plugin add`. A fresh clone has no `lib/` (it is built, not committed); the
`prepare` script builds it, so `pnpm install` is enough before starting the harness from source.
